# Implement block: Credit Card Flip Form (Jetpack Compose)

You are adding the "Credit Card Flip Form" block from Native Cook to the user's Android app. The block already exists as working Kotlin code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

A dark payment screen: "CHECKOUT · STEP 2 OF 2" over a bold "Card details" with the total, €248.00, on the right, a live card preview resting on a soft shadow tinted with its own light, four fields with their labels inside (Card number, Cardholder name, Expiry, CVV), a "Save card for next time" switch, a small lock line and a wide "Pay €248.00" pill that stays dark until the card is complete. The card is brushed metal: a fine horizontal grain and wavy guilloche over its colour, a soft light from above its top left, darker towards the bottom edge, a gold chip with a bright rim, a contactless mark, "HALCYON" and an empty dashed slot for the network, bullets for the sixteen digits, "YOUR NAME" and "MM/YY". Each digit typed rolls into place like a slot reel; the first digit names an invented network (Kestrel teal, Vela indigo, Orrery ember, Nimbus blue) whose mark pops into the corner while its colours spread across the card from it and the card swings to catch the light. A frame of light with a comet running round it hugs whichever part of the card is being edited and glides between the number, the name (growing with it) and the expiry, while one ring in the card's light colour glides between the fields below. Finished fields get a green check; an expiry in the past turns its field red as "Card expired". Focusing the CVV turns the card over to its back, with a magnetic stripe, the name signed in script and the frame of light round the CVV box. Dragging on the card tilts it in 3D and its light slides across the surface. Pay folds the button into a spinning ring and then a green circle with a check.

**Motion.** Each character on the card is a reel of its placeholder and the digits 0–9 twice: a typed digit spins down through a full run of digits to its place in 560 ms on a curve that overshoots a hair (0.16, 0.9, 0.3, 1.06), dimming to 55% while it moves; deleting spins it back in 420 ms, and clearing the card ripples the reels back from right to left 22 ms apart. When the first digit changes the network, the new gradient and glows spread from the network mark as a disc with a 26 pt soft edge over 900 ms on an ease-in-out curve (0.65, 0, 0.35, 1) while a 90 pt band of light tilted −22° crosses the card in 1.1 s, and the card swings 7° about its upright axis in 260 ms (ease-out 0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) then springs back flat (700 ms, damping ratio 0.55); the mark springs in from 0.7 scale (520 ms, ratio 0.62) as the old one fades and grows to 1.15 in 200 ms, with a selection haptic when typed by hand. Letters of the name rise 9 pt and grow from 0.86 in 300 ms (ease-out) and fade up when deleted. The frame of light on the card (1 pt hairline, 6% fill, 10 pt corners, standing 8 pt clear sideways and 7 pt above and below what it frames) and the ring on the form (1.5 pt) glide to the part being edited on one spring (520 ms, ratio 0.86) and fade in or out in 200 ms; a newly shown frame appears in place. The name and the expiry are measured, so the frame hugs them and grows with the name. A comet runs round the frame at an even speed, once every 2.6 s: a bright 1.75 pt head 12% of the perimeter long over a 34% tail at 40%. Dragging on the card tilts it towards the finger by 0.09° per pt, eased into ±12° about the upright axis and ±9° about the horizontal one, through 1100 pt perspective; the specular light slides against the tilt (half the card per 10°) and the shadow shifts the other way; on release it springs flat (700 ms, ratio 0.55) with the finger's speed. Focusing the CVV turns the card over on a spring (820 ms, ratio 0.74), lifting it 14 pt and growing it 5% at mid-turn, with a light haptic; the CVV's frame fades in over 220 ms in dark ink on the signature strip. Input is real: the number is grouped in fours, the name kept to capitals, the expiry written MM/YY (a first digit above 1 becomes 0x, months past 12 are refused) and the CVV kept to three digits; a complete number moves the keyboard to the name, the name's Next key to the expiry and a complete, valid expiry to the CVV; with the keyboard up the page rises just enough to keep the focused field 16 pt above it, and over the first 14 pt of that rise the big header fades out (smoothstep) while a compact bar pinned under the top inset (the title and the total in one 44 pt row, on the screen colour over a hairline) fades in and settles 6 pt, so nothing slides under the Dynamic Island: the page passes under the bar. Field checks pop in from 60% on a spring (380 ms, ratio 0.6) and leave in 140 ms; the expired state turns label and border red in 200 ms. The pay button lights from dark to white in 240 ms once the card is complete; pay folds it to a 56 pt circle in 380 ms, spins a ring at 820 ms a turn for 1.5 s, then fills green while a check draws in 380 ms, the light crosses the card again and a success haptic fires; 1.8 s later the form empties. The self-playing demo focuses the number at 0.6 s, types 5412 7534 8810 2697 from 0.95 s at about 150 ms a key, JONAH VERRIER from 3.8 s, 08/29 from 5.4 s, turns the card for the CVV at 6.4 s and types 417, turns it back at 7.9 s, presses Pay at 8.4 s and repeats every 14.2 s (LOOP); its caret blinks in the field it types into. Any touch on the card, a field, the switch or the button takes over, and the loop starts again from an empty form 4 s after the form is left alone. Under reduced motion the reels jump straight to their digits, the frame and ring jump between fields, the comet stands still, the card does not tilt or swing, it cross-fades to its back in 260 ms instead of turning, and the light does not cross it.

## Reference source

The block is built and running in the Native Cook source repository. Each link below is a file on GitHub. To read one as plain text, replace `https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/` in its address.

### Demo (start here)

- [CreditCardFlipFormDemo.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/forms/creditcardflipform/CreditCardFlipFormDemo.kt)

### Files of the block

- [CreditCardFlipForm.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/forms/creditcardflipform/CreditCardFlipForm.kt)
- [CreditCardFlipFormCard.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/forms/creditcardflipform/CreditCardFlipFormCard.kt)
- [CreditCardFlipFormEngine.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/forms/creditcardflipform/CreditCardFlipFormEngine.kt)

### Shared helpers the block uses

- [kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/shared/ComponentSupport.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/shared/ComponentSupport.kt)

### Libraries

It needs no library beyond a new Compose project.

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced Android engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on an emulator or a device. A Compose preview is useful while you work, but it is not the proof: build, install and run the app.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is an Android app built with Gradle. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- The app module, its namespace, `minSdk`, `compileSdk`, and the versions of Kotlin, the Android Gradle Plugin and Compose (a BOM or single versions).
- Whether Compose is switched on in that module, and whether screens are Compose, Views or both.
- Navigation: Navigation Compose, fragments, activities, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- How dependencies are declared: a version catalog (`libs.versions.toml`) or directly in `build.gradle`.
- Conventions: package layout, naming, theme, where resources live and how they are named.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file in the block's package. The list above names every file of the block, and the resources it uses from outside its package.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo shows, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's parameters and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's libraries and the versions it was built with to the host's. Add what is missing the way this project declares dependencies. Do not upgrade the host's Kotlin, Gradle plugin or Compose versions without asking; if an API differs on the host's version, adapt the block's code.
- Check `minSdk`. If the block uses an API newer than the host's minimum, keep the fallback the source has, or tell the user what would be lost.
- If Compose is not switched on in the module, say what turning it on involves before you do it. In a View-based screen, show the block through a `ComposeView`.
- Shared helpers: copy the ones the block imports next to it, or fold them into the block's files. Do not copy helpers it never calls.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files into a package of this app, and rewrite the `package` lines and the imports, including the import of the app's own `R` class.
- Copy its resources and asset files. Keep their names unless one collides with a resource of the app; then rename it everywhere it is used.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility descriptions as they are in the source. If the block needs a permission, add it to the manifest and say so.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or destination named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Build with the project's own task, for example `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug`, and fix every error and new warning the block introduced.
- Install and run it, and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with animations switched off in the system settings.
- If the build or the emulator fails for a reason outside the block, report the error and ask how to continue.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, dependencies and permissions added, and anything renamed to avoid a collision.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
